objective: Attack the primary diagnosis for hidden human routing, false safety assumptions, or accidental parallel scheduling.

corrections.finding: S001 listed the pre-durable watchdog among reused mechanisms, but its source note is CANDIDATE_LEARNING. It is a candidate UX/failure-detection repair, not a proven CURRENT capability.
corrections.correction: Treat the existing executable fallback as the canonical inline-authorized /wc human envelope plus existing durable worker/Guide mechanisms. Any watchdog implementation must remain observation-only until separately owned and verified.

corrections.finding: S001 correctly marked the authorization-envelope explanation as a strongest-supported hypothesis, not proof. The successful RUN beacon/claim shows GitHub writes are not globally blocked, but it does not prove a normal guide-PIN path will be accepted under the same inline authorization.
corrections.correction: The next fresh non-RUN canonical canary is the discriminator. If its beacon succeeds and the guide-PIN CREATE is explicitly safety-denied again, classify a path/tool-safety incompatibility rather than changing routing semantics.

hidden_human_routing_dependency.finding: The human remains a chat-wake boundary, but does not choose task, slot, project, Guide role, or priority. The canonical prompt is task-agnostic and machine routing remains downstream.

accidental_parallel_scheduler.finding: No queue, scheduler, CURRENT, worker family, or shadow router was added. A future pre-durable watchdog must only detect missing durable evidence and surface/escalate through existing mechanisms.

false_safety_assumption.finding: The exact durable facts are two explicit tool-layer safety outcomes. Missing inline authority is a plausible cross-attempt explanation, but path-specific guide-PIN sensitivity remains live until one canonical non-RUN canary tests it.

universal_prompt_semantics.finding: Restoration does not require adding task routing to the prompt. The existing canonical /wc envelope already separates generic bounded write authorization from machine-side task selection.

now_executable_without_architecture_chan: Treat only the existing canonical inline-authorized /wc envelope as executable write-authorizing universal entry.
Do not instruct the human to choose work. Preserve machine-side assignment.
After this RUN, the existing owner should replace any short launcher copy that omits the bounded authorization clause with the canonical envelope.
candidate_not_yet_current: Add a local/client pre-durable timeout state so Primary Chat never waits indefinitely for a beacon.
Allow at most one identical fresh-shell retry for an isolated pre-beacon failure, then escalate repeated friction via existing GUIDE_RESCATE.

discriminator_canary.required: Exactly one fresh non-RUN canonical /wc launch after the launcher surface emits the inline-authorized envelope.
discriminator_canary.pass_condition: Fresh beacon plus one valid normal authority claim.
discriminator_canary.fail_branch: If explicit guide-PIN safety denial repeats, preserve universal routing and repair the tool/path authority transport boundary; do not add a scheduler and do not ask the human to route.

evidence_map.evidence: S001 result + current RUN beacon/claim/STARTED successes + attempt-2 no-allocation receipt
No new control mechanism created; proposed watchdog explicitly non-authority.
Authorization clause carries scope, not routing; packet/allocator still owns assignment.

final_recommendation: Keep the universal prompt semantics. Fix/standardize the human-visible entry envelope so bounded authorization is inline, then run one canonical non-RUN discriminator canary. If guide-PIN safety still fails, repair that transport/path boundary under its existing owner instead of inventing routing.

resumable_checkpoint.next_action: Owner-backed launcher/control-surface change: emit canonical inline-authorized /wc text byte-for-byte wherever a short executable alias is currently surfaced, then run one fresh non-RUN canary.
